text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- 1996 MARKED NEW ERA FOR INDUSTRY
1996 marked a new phase for various sectors of Brazilian industry, which posted production and sales records to surpass those of peak years 1980 and 1986 and leave the "lost decade" behind.
-- BOLSAS LED IN EARNINGS LAST YEAR

Brazil's stock markets showed the best profitability of any financial investments in the country last year, with the Sao Paulo bolsa posting a 49.98 percent rise in real terms and the Rio de Janeiro bourse registering a 46.3 percent hike.
-- CARDOSO IS IN A HURRY: RE-ELECTION AND END OF 3/5 VOTE

Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has two priorities in 1997: win approval for his re-election bill and free himself of the three-fifths majority requirement in Congress to amend the constitution.
O GLOBO
-- RIO MAYOR TO SEEK CARDOSO, STATE HELP TO RUN CITY

Luiz Paulo Conde, took the reins as Rio de Janeiro's new mayor yesterday, said he would urgently appeal to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso for a 170 million-real federal loan and seek common ground with Rio state Governor Marcello Alencar over prickly tax and transit issues.
-- BRAZILIAN INDUSTRY OPENS FIRE ON IMPORTS
The opening of the Brazilian market to world goods has brought a rise in lawsuits against imported products. Of the 49 anti-dumping suits launched so far in Brazil, eight were begun in 1996.
-- SAO PAULO'S MALUF USES FAREWELL SPEECH TO SLAM CARDOSO

Some 5,000 Brazilian cities welcomed the New Year by installing new mayors. Celso Pitta took over at Sao Paulo city hall from outgoing mayor and presidential hopeful Paulo Maluf, who used his farewell speech to slam President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's economic policy.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- 4,700 UNREGULATED AIRCRAFT OPERATE IN BRAZIL

Half of Brazil's fleet of private aircraft and air taxis operate irregularly and 4,725 craft ought not to be flying. In 1996's first 11 months, 65 people died in 51 accidents involving executive aircraft versus 81 deaths in 68 crashes in 1995.
-- BRAZIL WILL PRODUCE 11 TYPES OF CARS BY 2000
By 2000, 11 automakers will operate plants in Brazil compared with four today. Honda, Toyota, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Chrysler, Renault and Asia Motors will join those already building cars here.
-- RIOT AT RIO JUVENILE HALL LEAVES ONE DEAD
A New Year's Eve uprising at a juvenile detention center in Rio de Janeiro left a 15-year-old boy dead and 39 youths injured while 23 others escaped in the mayhem.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
